newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU calls for democracy in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: EU calls for democracy in Cuba.

text.p: The European Union pledged on Saturday to push for democracy in Cuba, threatening to suspend any future trade agreement with Havana if it saw a serious breach of human rights.
At an EU summit in Dublin, leaders from the 15-nation bloc said they wanted to see political and economic improvements in Cuba.
"The EU wishes to see progress towards a peaceful transition to pluralist democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms in Cuba," the leaders said in their summit communique.
"(It also wishes to see) economic policies calculated to bring about a sustainable recovery and an improvement in the living standards of the Cuban people," it added.
It said it would consider negotiating a trade and co-operation agreement with Cuba but reminded Havana that in accordance with EU practices, such a pact could be suspended on human rights grounds.
Last week, the EU adopted a new formal strategy for its relations with Cuba, tieing relations closer to improvements in democracy.
Havana has reacted sharply to criticism from abroad, including rejecting Spain's new ambassador to the communist-led Caribbean island.
The new EU stance has been brought on in part as a reaction to the United States' Helms-Burton law, an amalgam of anti-Cuban legislation.
Washington wants its partners to take stronger action against Havana, but has infuriated most of them by threatening actions against foreign firms that do certain kinds of business on the island.

The EU leaders reiterated their objections to the Helms-Burton law, saying in a separate statement that promoting human rights in countries "should be pursued by means other than unilateral action at the expense of closer partners with shared values."
